notes: This theme came back nearly empty on GitHub's repo-search API. City/state-specific STR queries (Gatlinburg, Scottsdale, Sedona, Breckenridge, Smoky Mountains, Denver, Orlando) returned zero repos in every case; only generic 'airbnb florida' / 'airbnb texas' queries surfaced anything, and those three hits are all small single-vintage coursework/ML-tutorial repos (Tableau dashboards, an XGBoost price-prediction notebook) with no confirmed committed multi-file dataset, no stars, and thin descriptions -- exactly the kind of generic-boilerplate result the brief says to treat skeptically, so all three are rated low potential and none is confirmed to fill a numbered gap. I hit the 6-call hard limit on `gh search repos` before exhausting query variations (never tried topic-based `--topic=` searches, nor state-specific abbreviations like 'FL STR' or 'CO vacation rental', nor city names combined with 'occupancy tax' or 'lodging tax' which per gap #8 might have been more productive). A one-time `gh search code` for 'gatlinburg' returned only unrelated word-list/dictionary repos, not data files. WebSearch was already at its session-wide 200/200 budget before I could run any query for this theme (a shared budget across the concurrent scout swarm), and the two WebFetch attempts at github.com/search HTML pages both hit HTTP 429 (rate limited), so I could not substitute web search for the missing gh search calls. Net: this US sunbelt/mountain STR theme is very likely under-scouted relative to its actual GitHub footprint -- a rerun with fresh `gh search` and `WebSearch` budgets, and queries built around gap #8 (lodging/bed tax collections by city: Florida county tourist development tax, Colorado county sales/lodging tax open-data portals, Nevada/Clark County occupancy, Hawaii-style state tourism offices) and gap #12 (STR ordinance/registration trackers for Scottsdale, Sedona, Breckenridge/Summit County, Gatlinburg/Sevier County, and Florida's 2024 state preemption fight) would likely be far more productive than plain '<city> airbnb dataset' phrasing, since STR platforms rarely commit raw city-level data to GitHub but municipal open-data portals and academic STR-regulation trackers sometimes do.
